risk_reasons: Both write sites sit inside worker/jobs/response-generation/persist.ts, on the single sql.begin that carries invariant #4's moderation-hold atomicity. A ledger failure aborts the response persist itself.
The policy_gate_held lane records the auto-approval gate decision, so the change touches the approval path CLAUDE.md invariant #3 governs.
policy_gate_held is the highest-volume lane on the ledger. A wrong guard writes rows for every generated draft, or silently writes none.
The Refusal category is frozen at write and #1002 ruled there is never a backfill, so a wrong map value is not correctable by a later deploy.
goal: persistResponseAndNotify records a held_draft Refusal for a high-severity moderation flag, and a policy_gate_held Refusal for an auto-approval gate that held a genuine candidate draft for the owner, both on the transaction that made the decision.
non_goals: The five lanes shipped by #1009, #1010, #1011 and #1012. This slice adds no call site outside persist.ts.
The Restraint tab and any read over refusal_events. #1014 owns the read path.
Any migration. Migration 116 already admits both lanes, and #1001 deliberately rejected a CHECK pinning held_draft to unsafe_content.
Editing src/lib/refusals/write.ts. This slice consumes writeRefusalEvent as shipped by #1009.
Changing which drafts are held, which drafts auto-approve, or any auto-approval gate. This slice records the decision and alters none of it.
#998's proposed consistency test between AUTO_APPROVAL_BLOCK_PRECEDENCE and REFUSAL_CATEGORIES. #1003 ruled it must not be written; it fails on day one and making it pass breaks #995.
A drift test asserting that reordering REFUSAL_CATEGORIES cannot change a resolved category. #1003 declined it as a recorded owner call.
Reading auto_approval_policies for a structural non-candidate. Owner decision 2026-08-31: keep #998's narrowing verbatim.
Bumping REFUSAL_VOCABULARY_VERSION. This slice adds maps for two lanes that have written no rows; it re-maps no code that any stored row carries.
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible change. Nothing reads refusal_events until #1014.
A draft flagged high-severity writes one held_draft refusal_events row in the same transaction as its flagged_responses row.
A genuine auto-approval candidate the gate holds for the owner writes one policy_gate_held refusal_events row in the same transaction as the responses INSERT.
A draft that is not a genuine candidate writes no policy_gate_held row. With AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED off, that is every draft, so the lane is silent in production until the flag is turned on.
Setting REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false stops both writes without a deploy and leaves persist behaviour byte-identical to today.
invariants: The policy_gate_held write is guarded on !held ONLY. It never inherits the activeRun half of persist.ts's existing policy_gate step guard, because a legacy pre-spine review has no run and would silently drop rows from the highest-volume lane (#997 resolution 1).
A null-mapped member present anywhere in blockReasons suppresses the whole row, whatever its position. null is a veto, not a rank (#1003).

The category is read from AUTO_APPROVAL_BLOCK_PRECEDENCE, an explicit member constant, and never from REFUSAL_CATEGORIES order. Reading the category array would falsify #995's ruling that a reorder is presentation only.
One draft is one Refusal. One row per decision, never one per code.
The winning refusal_code is always a member of all_refusal_codes, which carries the full co-occurring set verbatim in blockReasons order. C5 enforces membership in storage.
held_draft writes refusal_code NULL and all_refusal_codes NULL. C4 makes that biconditional with the lane.
held_draft writes HELD_DRAFT_REFUSAL_CATEGORY, the literal unsafe_content, owned by src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts and deliberately not by a schema CHECK (#1001).
Both lanes write subject_type response and subject_id responseId, and both carry the accountId and businessId already in local scope.

occurredAt is the transaction-time sentinel on both lanes. policy_gate_held has no immutable stamp of its own (#997 F5), and held_draft's flagged_responses.created_at is DEFAULT NOW() in the same transaction, so both agree to the microsecond.

The policy_gate_held write inherits logAutoApprovalFallbackIfNeeded's candidacy narrowing verbatim: origin lane live_ingest_new AND effectivePolicy.threshold not null. It therefore requires a non-null runtimeState and adds no DB read.
resolvePolicyGateRefusal throws on a member present in neither the veto set nor the precedence list. An unrecognised code is a fault, not a category (CONTEXT.md, Refusal category).
Neither ledger write is caught at its call site. Both abort the persist transaction, and REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is the lever.
src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts stays a pure, client-safe leaf: every import remains import type, so nothing there can reach a runtime graph the Restraint tab would bundle.
Tenant isolation: every row carries account_id NOT NULL and refusal_events keeps deny-all RLS.
edge_cases: A high-severity flag writes one held_draft row and no policy_gate_held row, because held true suppresses the second lane entirely.
A review with no spine run still writes its policy_gate_held row. findActiveReviewRun returns null and the write does not consult it.

AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED is off: every draft is a structural non-candidate, runtimeState is null, and no policy_gate_held row is written. The ticket's and #1003's Volume prose describe a mechanism the code does not have; both are corrected on this branch.

The flag flips off between the pre-transaction isAutoApprovalCandidate read and the in-transaction evaluateAutoApprovalCandidate read: blockReasons carries auto_approval_disabled with a real runtimeState, and the row is written as autonomy_paused. This is the member's only live path.
An approved draft writes no policy_gate_held row. approved means blockReasons is empty.

A downgraded Autopilot account keeps its policy row, so a 2-star review yields autopilot_tier_required plus rating_below_positive_quadrant. The veto member suppresses the row, so the owner is never told we chose to send it to them.
A suspended week yields policy_suspended plus rating_below_threshold on many drafts. The precedence reports autonomy_paused, not owner_review_required.
A draft whose blockReasons contains only precedence members resolves to the highest tier present, with the stored code chosen by within-tier order.
The same response is persisted twice: the partial unique index on (refusal_source, subject_id) leaves one row per lane, and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING lets the second transaction commit.
held_draft and policy_gate_held share one subject_id but differ in refusal_source, so the partial unique index admits both. They never co-occur, because held vetoes the second.

REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false: the response INSERT, the flagged_responses row, the spine checkpoints, the auto-approval commit and the notification enqueue are all unchanged, and the helper emits one warning per disabled episode.
A CHECK violation from a writer bug aborts the persist transaction, so no response row lands and the generation job retries.
The content-freshness gate skips the persist before either write site is reached, so a stale draft writes no Refusal.

rollback_plan: Three layers. (1) REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false on Railway stops both writes with no deploy and leaves persist byte-identical to today; invoke the flag-flip skill. (2) Revert the PR on main and redeploy, which removes both call sites and the two vocabulary maps together. (3) No down migration: migration 116 stays and rows already written are not deleted. ArchivalPoller's refusal_events arm landed in #1009 and is untouched, so surviving rows still age out at REFUSAL_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS. Note that AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED is off in production, so the policy_gate_held lane writes nothing there until the go-live flip; the held_draft lane is live from the moment this merges.
observability: One warning per disabled episode from src/lib/refusals/write.ts whenever REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false.
A ledger failure here reaches Sentry through attachJobFailureSink on the terminal BullMQ attempt, because both sites run inside ResponseGeneratorWorker.

Reconciliation query for staging, held_draft: COUNT(*) of refusal_events WHERE refusal_source = 'held_draft' must EQUAL the count of flagged_responses rows for the same accounts inside the retention window. The two are written in one transaction under the same condition, so any inequality is a defect.

Reconciliation query for staging, policy_gate_held: COUNT(*) of refusal_events WHERE refusal_source = 'policy_gate_held' must be LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO the count of 'Auto-approval fallback to owner review' log lines for the same window. It is not an equality: the veto set suppresses rows the log still emits. A refusal count EXCEEDING the log count means a row was written for a draft the narrowing should have excluded.
Staging must run with AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED on to exercise the policy_gate_held lane at all. A staging ride with the flag off proves only the held_draft lane.
